TSM.name: TSMC
TSM.reported: NT$1,494.24B revenue · 66.4% gross margin · 58.7% operating margin
TSM.head: The broadest exposure to both Nvidia and custom chips
TSM.thesis: TSMC can earn wafer and advanced-packaging revenue whether the end customer chooses an Nvidia GPU, a hyperscaler ASIC or another merchant accelerator, provided TSMC wins those manufacturing and packaging steps. That makes customer-specific accelerator substitution a smaller risk here than for Nvidia.
points: October sales strengthen the near-term demand case

October revenue reached NT$586.89B, up 59.7% from a year earlier. January–October sales rose 43.3%. Q3 net margin was 51.1% and diluted EPS was US$4.60 per ADR. All of October's sales are consolidated, so the AI share cannot be inferred from the monthly number.

Revenue rose 50.9% in Taiwan dollars and 41.2% in US dollars year over year. Management guided Q4 to US$52.3–54.3B revenue, 65–67% gross margin and 56.5–58.5% operating margin. The Q3 margin declined sequentially as N2 ramped.

Management described continued leading-edge supply pressure and three additional fabs to support the multiyear N3 pipeline. N2 ramps alongside N3 and advanced packaging. TSMC discusses demand visibility and capacity plans. The public materials do not supply a customer-by-customer noncancelable AI backlog.

FY2025 operating cash flow was NT$2,275.0B and gross PP&E purchases were NT$1,272.4B, leaving NT$1,002.6B before other investing and financing. Management expects overseas fab dilution of roughly 3–4 percentage points over the next few years. The major decisions are how much capacity to build and how quickly new nodes and overseas fabs reach profitable utilization.

Export restrictions can shrink or delay eligible downstream demand. Node leadership and customer diversification support reallocation if buyers have qualified designs and power. Taiwan concentration remains a structural risk, and geographic duplication has a cost.
TSM.assumption: Normalized 2027 annual earnings in US dollars per NYSE ADR. Five Taiwan common shares equal one ADR. The model uses 25.93B local shares, or 5.186B ADR equivalents. Dollar revenue and dollar earnings use the same currency, so there is no second FX conversion. Taiwan-dollar appreciation can still squeeze translated margins.

model.reason: An N2 yield shortfall, excess overseas capacity and a pause in customer installations depress utilization. Sales slip below four times Q4 guided revenue and net margin falls to 40%.

The midpoint of Q4 guidance implies US$213.2B annualized sales. Flat revenue around that level and a 47% net margin allow for startup and overseas costs. At 20×, shareholders pay a 5% earnings yield for durable node leadership.
N2 scales profitably and advanced packaging stays tight across GPUs and custom chips. Sales grow beyond the Q4 run rate while the 50% margin approaches Q3’s 51.1%.

TSM.basis: Normalized 2027 annual earnings in US dollars per NYSE ADR. Five Taiwan common shares equal one ADR. The model uses 25.93B local shares, or 5.186B ADR equivalents. Dollar revenue and dollar earnings use the same currency, so there is no second FX conversion. Taiwan-dollar appreciation can still squeeze translated margins.
TSM.why: Best balance of diversified demand and downside in this group. The foundry can win whichever accelerator design wins, provided it retains the process and packaging orders.
TSM.trigger: Revisit if Q4 sales fall below $52.3B or operating margin falls below the 56.5% guidance floor. If that happens despite rising wafer volumes, overseas cost and yield dilution deserve a larger haircut.
TSM.multipleRationale: 15× reflects underused new fabs and persistent geopolitical risk. Paying 24× assumes leadership survives the spending ramp and customers absorb the new capacity.

AVGO.name: Broadcom
AVGO.reported: $29.591B revenue · $15.955B GAAP operating profit · $2.68 GAAP diluted EPS
AVGO.head: Custom silicon offers upside, with growing credit exposure
AVGO.thesis: Hold at $304.41. Custom AI accelerators and switching can capture spending that moves off merchant GPUs. The software business and strong cash generation support the base case. A concentrated customer program can move shipments materially, and supporting its financing ties hardware margins to counterparty credit and resale values.
points: Q3 AI semiconductor sales were $16.7B, up 221% year over year and 56.4% of group revenue. Revenue was $29.591B, GAAP net income $13.088B and operating cash flow $14.197B. Q4 guidance was $34.8B revenue, $21.7B AI semiconductor sales and roughly 66% non-GAAP operating margin. At the Q4 midpoint the implied FY2026 revenue is $105.889B using the reported nine months.

In the Q3 call management put FY2027 and FY2028 AI semiconductor revenue outlook at approximately $115B and $230B. The outlook depends on availability of leading-edge wafers, memory, substrates and energized facilities. VMware software and conventional semiconductors diversify cash generation. AI volume growing faster than high-margin infrastructure software lowers the group gross-margin mix, even with operating leverage.

The June arrangement had a $29B maximum potential residual-value liability at full deployment. The October agreement cited a further $43B undiscounted maximum and a 72.5% lease-balance reference, net of rack sale proceeds upon default. Maximum exposure is distinct from booked loss or expected payout. A November 20 supply-chain survey by Ming-Chi Kuo estimated a roughly 20% cut to Google’s planned 2027 Broadcom-designed TPU 8i volume. Neither partner confirmed the estimate in these disclosures. A mix shift to another design can hurt Broadcom even as aggregate TPU demand grows.

The next earnings update is December 9. Compare the $21.7B AI guide with actual shipments and listen for changes to FY27 customer ramps. Track cash collections and growth of guarantees alongside revenue. An earnings miss coupled with new guarantees makes the bear case more plausible. Q3 operating cash less gross capex was $13.665B despite the exposure.
AVGO.financialNote: FY2021 reported $27M of preferred stock dividend obligation between liabilities and equity. Assets equal reported liabilities plus stockholders’ equity plus that obligation. The FY2024 VMware acquisition changes period comparability.
AVGO.horizon: Normalized FY2027 group earnings, fiscal year ending around November 2027. Net margin after interest, tax, stock compensation and ordinary amortization.
AVGO.assumption: Group revenue is modeled from AI plus all other business. Q3 FY26 GAAP net margin was 44.2%. The model uses 4.90 billion diluted shares, near the reported 4.887 billion. Group bears credit and mix risk. The 18×/24×/30× earnings multiples imply net earnings yields of 5.6%/4.2%/3.3%. They value weaker durability, continued growth or sustained high growth, respectively.

MRVL.name: Marvell Technology
MRVL.reported: $2.739B revenue · $459.7M GAAP operating profit · $0.33 GAAP diluted EPS
MRVL.head: A cheaper price still requires a strong standalone ramp
MRVL.thesis: Wait for operating leverage or a wider discount. Network connectivity and custom silicon participate in both GPU and ASIC deployments. The normal case requires standalone margins to rise substantially, and the pending all-stock Lumentum deal introduces approval, dilution and integration risks.
points: Q2 data center sales were $2.172B, 79% of group sales and up 46% year over year. GAAP gross margin was 53.1%, GAAP net income $308.0M and CFO $605.5M. Q3 guidance was $3.15B ±5%, GAAP EPS $0.53 ±$0.05 and non-GAAP EPS $1.10 ±$0.05. Management’s October investor day showed standalone FY2027 revenue of $12B and FY2028 revenue of $20B.

Marvell signed a Google agreement for custom silicon in the TPU ecosystem, including inference accelerators and network and memory controllers. Google received warrants for up to 58.97M shares at $206.58 with vesting conditions. Nvidia invested $2B and partnered on NVLink Fusion. Neither an equity investment nor a design agreement reveals committed annual chip revenue. Actual system builds and content per cluster determine sales.

On November 2 Marvell disclosed an all-stock agreement for Lumentum. The exchange ratio is 4.5 MRVL shares per Lumentum share, giving existing Marvell holders about 67% of the combined business. Closing is expected in the first half of calendar 2028 subject to approvals. Management targets $1B+ of run-rate synergies and non-GAAP EPS accretion in the first year after closing. Our November 2027 scenarios use standalone sales and shares throughout, with deal uncertainty reflected in the multiple.

FY2026 net income included a $1.8B pre-tax gain on the automotive Ethernet sale. Historical net profit will overstate repeatable earnings if that gain is carried forward. Q2 stock-based compensation was $326M, over 10% of sales. GAAP Q3 EPS guidance at its midpoint implies approximately 15.5% net margin using guided diluted shares. The normal model needs 22%. December 1 results will test conversion of the custom ramp, pricing and operating leverage.
MRVL.financialNote: FY2026 net income and investing cash flow include the automotive Ethernet sale. FY2026 net income includes the $1.8B pre-tax sale gain. January/early February fiscal year-end.
MRVL.horizon: Standalone normalized FY2028 earnings for the year ending near January 2028, approximately two months after the target date. Margin models recurring net income to common, including stock compensation and recurring acquired amortization, excluding sale gains.
MRVL.assumption: Q2 reported 921.2M diluted shares. Model allows 930–950M for awards and other ordinary dilution, with more in the bull case. It does not count the contingent Google warrants at full face value. At November 20 the $206.58 strike exceeded market price. The projected 1H CY28 Lumentum closing follows the valuation date. 22×/30×/36× earnings correspond to 4.5%/3.3%/2.8% yields across execution outcomes.

005930.KS.name: Samsung Electronics
005930.KS.head: Memory earnings dominate while advanced foundry remains a separate bet
005930.KS.thesis: Samsung has exposure to memory, HBM base dies and outsourced logic manufacturing. The value of foundry share gains depends on 2 nm yields and external orders converting to profitable wafer volume. Its group profit also includes mobile, displays, consumer electronics and Harman.
points: Value the common shares after allocating preferred earnings

Q3 basic common EPS was ₩11,462 and diluted common EPS was ₩11,260. The ₩75.21T of profit attributable to owners includes preferred shareholders. The diluted common-share numerator was ₩66.08T across 5.87B shares. The model allocates 88% of owners’ profit to common shareholders. The quarterly ₩4,601 dividend is excluded from price returns.

Device Solutions reported ₩147.1T quarterly revenue and ₩106.5T operating profit, close to 99% of consolidated operating profit. Device eXperience reported a ₩0.8T operating loss. Samsung reported Q3 common EPS of ₩11,462 in its reviewed quarterly statements.

Management reported higher HBM4 sales, server SSD demand and 2 nm HPC foundry wins, plus HBM base-die growth. FY2026 capex is expected around ₩84.4T, of which ₩76.8T is Device Solutions. Nvidia shipment allocations, order prices and full foundry backlog remain undisclosed in these materials.

FY2025 operating cash flow was ₩85.3T and gross PP&E outlays were ₩47.5T, implying ₩37.8T on the common definition. In 2023, the same calculation was −₩13.5T. Samsung indicated ₩90–110T of estimated 2026 shareholder returns. That figure reflects management’s plan and should be compared with recurring free cash flow after investment.

Track volume-qualified HBM customers, 2 nm yield and customer diversity, cash conversion after capex, and the effect of higher memory costs on devices. Its broad business mix can reduce reliance on one customer, while consolidated margin hides foundry and memory economics.
005930.KS.assumption: Normalized 2027 annual owners’ earnings. Common-share EPS = group revenue × owners’ net margin × 88% common allocation ÷ 5.87B diluted common shares. ₩T divided by billions of shares is multiplied by 1,000 to produce won per share.

model.reason: Memory prices reset, device margins stay weak and 2 nm yields disappoint. ₩480T revenue and a 22% margin reflect a pronounced fall from Q3.
₩650T revenue is below the ₩781T annualized Q3 pace. A 33% owners’ margin allows pricing to normalize while HBM volumes grow and device losses narrow.
HBM4 scales with external customers, devices recover and foundry losses narrow. ₩790T sales and 40.5% owners’ margin require performance above the Q3 owners’ margin of 38.5%.

005930.KS.basis: Normalized 2027 annual owners’ earnings. Common-share EPS = group revenue × owners’ net margin × 88% common allocation ÷ 5.87B diluted common shares. ₩T divided by billions of shares is multiplied by 1,000 to produce won per share.
005930.KS.why: The close prices in substantial memory normalization. The higher upside comes with exposure to foundry execution, mobile losses and a large capex budget.
005930.KS.trigger: Monitor Device Solutions operating profit alongside mobile and foundry economics. An HBM qualification announcement without profitable volume, or buybacks funded by weaker cash generation, would weaken the rerating case.
005930.KS.multipleRationale: 7× reflects foundry losses and a commodity recovery that stalls. 11× needs sustained group profitability and shareholder distributions funded from operating cash.

MU.name: Micron
MU.reported: $54.23B revenue · 86.8% GAAP gross margin · $32.87 diluted EPS
MU.head: The clearest memory price and customer-deposit disclosures
MU.thesis: Micron’s exposure spans HBM, server DRAM and enterprise SSDs. It can benefit from Nvidia or ASIC deployments if the relevant memory is qualified. Contract coverage helps make FY2027 visible, while valuation remains highly sensitive to memory pricing after new supply arrives.
points: Q4 revenue was $54.229B versus $11.315B a year earlier. GAAP diluted EPS was $32.87. Q1 FY2027 guidance was $61.5B ± $1.5B in revenue, about 85.95% GAAP gross margin and $37.84 ± $1.00 GAAP diluted EPS.

Management says agreements cover the vast majority of CY2027 HBM bit supply, at materially higher year-over-year prices. Its broader strategic customer agreements have multi-year take-or-pay features, and commitments from customers totaled $32B, mostly deposits. Deposits are cash received or committed under arrangements and do not measure recognized chip revenue or Nvidia’s share.

FY2026 operating cash flow was $89.675B against $30.712B gross PP&E purchases, leaving $58.963B on the common chart definition. Micron reported $62.31B adjusted FCF using $27.37B net capex. The difference follows the capex definition. New Idaho, Taiwan and Singapore capacity is expected to come on at different times, with meaningful construction spending ahead of full output.

Check signed bit volumes versus prices on open exposure, HBM4 qualification and yields, the amount of customer cash already collected, and working capital. FY2023’s $5.83B net loss illustrates how quickly operating leverage can reverse if memory prices weaken.
MU.assumption: Normalized annual earnings power at November 2027, in US dollars per diluted share. We use 1.15B diluted shares versus 1.147B in Q4. FY2026 net margin was 63.8%. The base assumes lower pricing after new supply and avoids extrapolating the next guided quarter.

model.reason: DRAM and NAND prices and HBM mix weaken together. A 30% net margin leaves profits positive even though FY2023 shows a full-cycle loss is possible.
Revenue of $195B exceeds FY2026 sales by 46% and sits 21% below the $246B annualized next-quarter guidance midpoint. A 50% net margin prices in substantial normalization.
Advanced memory remains scarce. The guided sales pace persists for a year and 68% net margin approaches the reported Q4 level of 69.5%.

MU.basis: Normalized annual earnings power at November 2027, in US dollars per diluted share. We use 1.15B diluted shares versus 1.147B in Q4. FY2026 net margin was 63.8%. The base assumes lower pricing after new supply and avoids extrapolating the next guided quarter.
MU.why: The normal case offers upside, but the bear case can roughly halve the shares. A low forward multiple is common near the top of a memory cycle.
MU.trigger: Watch realized HBM prices and bits separately, customer deposits versus receivables, and gross capex against operating cash flow. A miss below the $60B low end of the next revenue guide would weaken near-term support.
MU.multipleRationale: 8–12× acknowledges high capital requirements and cycles. The 12× best case needs structural pricing power beyond one booked year.

000660.KS.name: SK hynix
000660.KS.head: The strongest disclosed two-year capacity coverage of the memory group
000660.KS.thesis: SK hynix benefits directly from HBM per accelerator and indirectly from server DRAM and enterprise SSD demand. The value of its HBM lead depends on packaging yields, qualification across buyers, and keeping more of the economics as Samsung and Micron qualify rival products.
points: Use the November filing to distinguish operating earnings from investment gains

The November 16 SEC filing reports Q3 diluted EPS of ₩54,454 on 722.35M weighted diluted shares, and ₩145.63T of operating cash flow for nine months. Kioxia-linked gains can make attributable earnings volatile. The announced ₩20,000 Q3 dividend includes a ₩10,000 special component. A repeat special dividend is excluded from the share-price cases.

Revenue rose 32% sequentially and operating profit rose 38%. Management expects HBM4 to exceed HBM3E in shipments and revenue in Q4 and plans to bring M15X to maximum capacity by year-end. Quarterly net profit was meaningfully below operating profit. Use the quarterly report and normalized cash taxes for a run-rate assessment.

Long-term agreements covered more than 50% of 2027–28 total production capacity. The company describes price ranges that can adjust with market conditions. That disclosure improves volume visibility, while prices, delivery schedules, and buyer allocations still depend on contracts that are largely private.

SK hynix reported ₩114.5T cash and equivalents and ₩15.8T borrowings at September 30. FY2025 operating cash flow was ₩53.37T versus gross PP&E purchases of ₩27.52T. Management intends to increase investment materially. Annual margins swung from a loss in 2023 to about 49% in 2025, which puts the latest 80% quarterly margin in context.

Watch HBM4 yields, M15X output, competition on HBM4/HBM4E, reuse of capacity if pricing falls, China equipment licensing and new U.S. packaging execution. Take-or-pay volume or contractual price floors improve visibility only within the actual terms.
000660.KS.assumption: Normalized 2027 profit available to common shareholders in KRW, excluding separate gains on Kioxia and incremental special payouts. We model 722M diluted shares versus 722.35M reported in Q3. The normalized margin is common earnings divided by consolidated revenue.

model.reason: New supply cuts contract prices and customer qualification slips. ₩220T sales and 19.5% normalized margin still leave substantial operating earnings.
Volume agreements cushion the downside, but pricing resets and capex rise. ₩300T revenue is 28% below annualized Q3 sales. The model retains 27.8% as normalized common earnings.
HBM4 leadership endures across multiple customers. ₩365T revenue and a 35.6% normalized margin approach Q3 reported profitability while excluding a separate Kioxia premium.

000660.KS.basis: Normalized 2027 profit available to common shareholders in KRW, excluding separate gains on Kioxia and incremental special payouts. We model 722M diluted shares versus 722.35M reported in Q3. The normalized margin is common earnings divided by consolidated revenue.
000660.KS.why: Its 2027–28 capacity coverage is the clearest of the three memory suppliers. At the current share price, investors already need most of the normal earnings case.
000660.KS.trigger: The thesis strengthens if HBM4 volumes overtake HBM3E on schedule and contract price bands protect profits as M15X ramps. Failing either test makes a 10× normalized multiple difficult to sustain.
000660.KS.multipleRationale: 7× discounts two years of pricing pressure. 12× requires sustained HBM leadership and customer diversification. Volume contracts with variable prices support a middle multiple.
